name: tower-endpoint-suspension
instr:
Please add reversible endpoint suspension to Tower's discovery and readiness machinery in `/app`. We need to take an endpoint out of routing temporarily without losing its service instance or interrupting responses already in flight. Don't add new crates.

Extend `tower::discover::Change<K, V>` with variants `tower::discover::Change::Suspend(K)` and `tower::discover::Change::Resume(K)`. The constant, pending-requests, and peak-EWMA discovery adapters should forward these events, and `tower::balance::p2c::Balance` should apply them to its endpoints.

Add methods `tower::ready_cache::ReadyCache::suspend<Q: Hash + Equivalent<K>>(&mut self, key: &Q) -> bool` and `tower::ready_cache::ReadyCache::resume<Q: Hash + Equivalent<K>>(&mut self, key: &Q) -> bool`, with the same enclosing bounds as `push`. Here `Equivalent` is the existing `tower::ready_cache::cache::Equivalent`. Return true only when a known key changes suspension state.

A suspended endpoint stays in the cache but is absent from the ready set and must not have its service polled or called. Suspension follows the key across replacements until resume or eviction; if an older ready instance and a pending replacement coexist when suspended, discard the older instance. Unknown keys do not acquire suspension state. Resuming schedules a fresh readiness check and wakes the task driving the cache. Suspended endpoints count as pending, so `poll_pending` remains pending while any are suspended. Eviction clears suspension for subseq
